clinicalPearls: A rare congenital absence of the crystalline lens, present from birth
Primary aphakia reflects failure of lens induction with severe anterior segment dysgenesis
Secondary aphakia occurs when a lens that did form is resorbed or extruded during development
It causes high hyperopia and is a cause of visual deprivation and amblyopia in the affected eye
It is frequently accompanied by other ocular malformations such as microphthalmia and anterior segment dysgenesis
Management focuses on optical correction and aggressive amblyopia therapy during the critical period
reference.pathophysiology: Congenital aphakia results from disturbance of lens development. In primary aphakia the surface ectoderm fails to differentiate into lens placode and vesicle, so no lens forms and the anterior segment develops abnormally. In secondary aphakia a lens is initially formed but is subsequently resorbed or expelled in utero, for example after intrauterine inflammation or with other developmental anomalies. Absence of the lens removes a major refractive element, producing marked hyperopia and, without correction, dense form-deprivation amblyopia.
additionalDifferentials: Anterior lenticonus or severe lens coloboma
Ectopia lentis with a dislocated lens out of the visual axis
additionalInvestigations: Examination and imaging (for example ultrasound biomicroscopy) to confirm lens absence
Assessment for associated anterior segment dysgenesis and microphthalmia
Genetic evaluation where syndromic features are present
redFlags: Dense amblyopia risk requiring urgent optical correction
Associated glaucoma or other sight-threatening malformation
Bilateral involvement affecting overall visual development
Syndromic features suggesting a broader disorder
reference.prognosis: Visual prognosis depends on the severity of associated malformations and on the timeliness of optical correction and amblyopia therapy, and is often guarded, particularly in primary aphakia.
pitfalls: Delaying optical correction and losing the amblyopia treatment window
Missing associated glaucoma or anterior segment dysgenesis
references: Taylor and Hoyt's Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
management: Correct the high aphakic hyperopia optically with spectacles or contact lenses to provide a focused retinal image
Institute aggressive amblyopia therapy with occlusion of the better-seeing eye during the critical period of visual development
Consider secondary intraocular lens implantation where the eye is anatomically suitable
Assess and manage associated anterior segment dysgenesis and microphthalmia, monitoring for glaucoma
Undertake regular refraction and visual development assessment
Offer genetic evaluation and counselling where syndromic features are present, with paediatric ophthalmology follow-up
